youtube.title: Why An Octopus Has Three Hearts 🐙 #Shorts
youtube.description:
An octopus has three hearts. And one of them stops when it swims.

Two small hearts pump blood through its gills, where it picks up oxygen. The third heart pushes that blood around the rest of its body. Its blood isn't red. It's blue, because it carries oxygen with copper, not iron. Copper carries far less oxygen than iron, so the octopus needs the extra pumps. But when it swims, that main heart stops beating. That's why octopuses would rather crawl. Swimming literally takes their breath away.

Watch our full episodes on the channel.
